questions.explanation: In transplatin the two chlorides are opposite, so the angle is 180 degrees. 90 degrees would be cisplatin.

questions.topic: Tetrahedral against square planar four-coordinate centres
questions.learningObjective: State the bond angle for tetrahedral geometry
questions.stem: A survey records the bond angle of a tetrahedral complex in degrees; what value is reported?
questions.explanation: The tetrahedral bond angle is 109.5 degrees. 90 degrees is square planar.

questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.topic: Bond angles in the two four-coordinate geometries
questions.learningObjective: State the bond angle for square planar geometry
questions.stem: A survey records the bond angle of a square planar complex in degrees; what value is reported?
questions.explanation: The square planar bond angle is 90 degrees. 109.5 degrees is tetrahedral.

questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.topic: Bond angles in an octahedron
questions.learningObjective: State the adjacent bond angle in an octahedron
questions.stem: A survey records the adjacent bond angle in a regular octahedron; what value is reported?
questions.explanation: Adjacent bonds in an octahedron are 90 degrees apart. 180 degrees is the opposite angle.

questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.topic: Why a d8 ion favours square planar geometry
questions.learningObjective: Explain why d8 favours square planar geometry
questions.stem: A survey note asks why d8 ions such as Pt2+ favour square planar geometry

answer.exemplar: Square planar geometry gives d8 ions greater crystal field stabilisation because the highest d orbital remains empty, whereas tetrahedral splitting would leave electrons in higher-energy orbitals.

questions.explanation: The empty highest orbital gives extra stabilisation. Tetrahedral would be less favourable for d8.
